messages.subject: Hidden Markov model with continuous measurements of observed sequence
parts:
Hi all,

Attached is a piece of code for a 2-state homogeneous Hidden Markov Model with Gaussian emission density. Basically, the observation y_t given hidden state s_t=i follows a Gaussian distribution with mean mu_i and standard deviation sigma_i, and the states have a transition probability matrix of gamma. 

However, an error was raised in the forward probability function, i.e., dmyHMM, with the message:
Error in probObs[state, state, time] <- (1/sqrt(2 * pi * (sigma[state])^2)) * : object 'probObs' not found

The probObs is meant to be defined as a matrix, with normal distribution densities on diagonals. Given the error message, I'm lost on where to define the probObs object. The attached code was one option that I tried, another try was to include probObs in the nimbleModel of homo.hmm, and treat it as a parameter in dmyHMM, but it also failed with a similar error message. 

Any suggestions, comments or questions are welcomed, thanks much in advance!

# forward probabilities
dmyHMM <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), # observations
                 probInit = double(1), # initial state probabilities
                 mu = double(1), # emission means
                 sigma = double(1), # emission standard deviations
                 probTrans = double(2), # transition probabilities
                 len = double(0, default = 0), # length of observation
                 log = integer(0, default = 0)
  ){
    for (time in 1:len) {
      # no deterministic assignment is allowed, but why?
      for (state in 1:3){
        #probObs[state, state, time] <- dnorm(x[time], mean = mu[state], sd = sigma[state])
        probObs[state, state, time] <- (1/sqrt(2*pi*(sigma[state])^2))*exp(-(x[time]-mu[state])^2/(2*sigma[state]^2))
      }
    }
   
    # forward probabilities
    ## at time point 1
    alpha <- probInit[1:3] %*% probObs[1:3, 1:3, 1]
    ## at time points 2:T
    for (time in 2:len) {
      # matrix multiplication:
      # forward at t = forward at t-1 %*% transition probabilities %*% emission probabilities
      alpha[1:3] <- (alpha[1:3] %*% probTrans[1:3,1:3]) %*% probObs[1:3, 1:3, time]
    }
    logL <- log(sum(alpha[1:3]))
    returnType(double(0))
    if (log) return(logL)
    return(exp(logL))
  }
)

rmyHMM <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(n = double(), # observations
                 probInit = double(1), # initial state probabilities
                 mu = double(1), # emission means
                 sigma = double(1), # emission standard deviations
                 probTrans = double(2), # transition probabilities
                 len = double(0, default = 0) # length of observation
  ) {
    returnType(double(1))
    s <- numeric(len)
    s[1] <- rcat(n = 1, prob = probInit[1:2])
    y <- s
    y[1] <- rnorm(n = 1, mean = mu[s[1]], sd = sigma[s[1]])
    for (t in 2:len){
      # state at t given state at t-1
      s[t] <- rcat(n = 1, prob = probTrans[s[t-1],1:2])
      # observation at t given state at t
      y[t] <- rnorm(n = 1, mean = mu[s[t]], sd = sigma[s[t]])
    }
    return(y)
  })
   
# assign NIMBLE function to the global R environment
assign('dmyHMM', dmyHMM, .GlobalEnv)
assign('rmyHMM', rmyHMM, .GlobalEnv)

homo.hmm <- nimbleCode({
 
  # priors
  ## initial probabilities
  delta[1] ~ dunif(0, 1)
  delta[2] <- 1 - delta[1]
  ## transition probabilities
  gamma[1, 1] ~ dunif(0, 1)
  gamma[1, 2] <- 1 - gamma[1, 1]
  gamma[2, 1] ~ dunif(0, 1)
  gamma[2, 2] <- 1 - gamma[2, 1]
 
  for(state in 1:2){
    # prior for mean
    mu[state] ~ dgamma(1,1)
    # prior for variance
    sigma[state] ~ dinvgamma(1,1)
  }

  # likelihood
  y[1:T_len] ~ dmyHMM(
    probInit = delta[1:2]
    , mu = mu[1:2] # observation means
    , sigma = sigma[1:2] # observation standard deviation
    , probTrans = gamma[1:2,1:2] # transition matrix
    , len = T_len # nb of sampling occasions
  )
 
})

# observations
y <- c(8.80, 12.00, 10.93,  8.71,  9.49, 10.97, 10.71, 10.64,  9.60,  9.79,
 4.98,  6.92,  6.54,  4.36, 11.40, 10.78, 15.21,  5.35,  5.20,  7.96,
 5.85,  6.94,  7.49,  6.67,  5.69,  5.31,  3.27,  5.22,  4.06,  2.59,
 6.02,  5.30,  6.90,  7.45,  8.84,  5.68,  4.98,  7.02,  5.92,  5.24,
 7.01,  5.74,  3.71,  2.18,  2.06,  1.17,  2.06,  1.74,  2.48,  1.89,
 1.60,  2.88,  5.77,  4.82,  5.29,  5.55,  6.83,  5.63,  7.10,  4.52,
 5.10,  4.66,  5.50,  7.61,  4.16,  1.88,  1.49,  1.64,  1.95,  2.47,
 1.88,  2.72,  5.35,  8.95,  6.27,  7.14,  3.18,  6.15,  6.12,  6.49,
 7.33,  5.25,  6.32,  5.11,  5.41,  5.16,  5.99,  6.43, 11.03, 11.60,
 4.02, 10.57, 12.34, 13.85, 11.79, 11.50, 12.53, 12.37,  9.90,  9.46)

# constants
constants <- list(
  # number of observations
  T_len = length(y)
)
# data
data <- list(y = y)
# initial values
initial.values <- function() {
  list(
    # delta = rdirch(1, alpha = c(1,1))
    # , gamma = rbind(rdirch(1, alpha = c(1,1))
    #               , rdirch(1, alpha = c(1,1)))
    #               )
    delta = c(0.5, 0.5)
    , gamma = t(matrix(rep(c(0.5, 0.5), 2), 2, 2))
    # tpm_alpha = rep(runif(1, min = 0, max = 5), 3)
    , mu = rnorm(2, 2, 5)
    , sigma = rnorm(2, 2, 1)
  )
}

# parameters to save
parameters.to.save <- c("delta", "gamma", "mu", "sigma")

# MCMC details
n.iter <- 5000
n.burnin <- 1000
n.chains <- 2

mcmc.output <- nimbleMCMC(
  code = homo.hmm,
  constants = constants,
  data = data,
  inits = initial.values,
  monitors = parameters.to.save,
  niter = n.iter,
  nburnin = n.burnin,
  nchains = n.chains
  )

parts:
Dear Jaysen,

Apologies that your message slipped by for a while with no attention. We try to keep up but sometimes we fall behind.  Thanks for posting the question.
Inside a nimbleFunction, you can create a new multivariate object with syntax similar to R. You can do
probObs <- nimArray(dim = c(3, 3, len)) # or you can use "array" and it will be converted to "nimArray"
Information on this and related features is in section 11.2 of the User Manual (r-nimble.org)

Also, there are versions of HMMs implemented in the nimbleEcology package, with a vignette that goes over how to use them. You might need something more specific, but I just wanted to point it out.

It looks like you are populating only diagonal elements of probObs[1:3, 1:3, time] for each time, so you could perhaps just create a vector and use component-wise multiplication instead of matrix multiplication (or perhaps you are building up to more complicated cases where you need the full matrix).

HTH.

Perry

parts:
Thanks Perry! I'm developing a simpler version of HMM with continuous measurements (which is not offered in nimbleEcology package I believe), but aiming at a more complicated model in the future, so your mentioning about  nimArray  is helping a lot. 

I was able to solve the problem by defining  probObs  as a vector (instead of a matrix, for now), the updated code is attached below. After fixing this, probObs can be defined deterministically as a normal density without warning.

However, I'm having a new issue emerged with the error message below,
[Note] Infinite values were detected in model variable: logProb_y.

While I'm figuring out if it arises from the forward algorithm (in nimbleFunction dmyHMM), which I highly suspect, or prior specification, any advise or help is greatly appreciate!

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

dmyHMM <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), # observations
                 probInit = double(1), # initial state probabilities
                 mu = double(1), # emission means
                 sigma = double(1), # emission standard deviations
                 probTrans = double(2), # transition probabilities
T_len = double(0, default = 0), # length of observation

log = integer(0, default = 0)
  ){
## at time point 1

probObs <- numeric(2)

    # log forward probability
    alpha <- numeric(2)
    # accumulator
    alpha_out <- numeric(2)
   
    for (state in 1:2){
      probObs[state] <- dnorm(x[1], mean = mu[state], sd = sigma[state])
      alpha[state] <- log(probInit[state]) + log(probObs[state])

}
    ## at time points 2:T

for (time in 2:T_len) {
      for(state_in in 1:2){ # current state
        # emission density for observation at current time point
        probObs[state_in] <- dnorm(x[time], mean = mu[state_in], sd = sigma[state_in])
       
        for(state_out in 1:2){ # previous state
          alpha_out[state_out] <- alpha[state_out] + log(probTrans[state_out, state_in]) + log(probObs[state_in])
        }
        alpha[state_in] <- log(sum(exp(alpha_out[1:2])))
      }
    }
    logL <- log(sum(exp(alpha[1:2])))

returnType(double(0))
    if (log) return(logL)
    return(exp(logL))
  }
)

messages.subject: Re: Hidden Markov model with continuous measurements of observed sequence
parts:
I usually debug this kind of issue using the uncompiled model and investigating log prob calculations for narrower pieces of the model.

E.g. (making up variable names rather than using yours)
m <- nimbleModel(<your args>)
m$calculate() # Inf or -Inf warning
m$calculate('beta') # see if beta calculates ok
m$calculate('beta[1,]') # see if part of beta calculates ok
m$alpha # investigate values in the model, e.g. parameters used in beta
etc.

HTH
Perry
On Tue, Jul 18, 2023 at 2:05 PM 'Jaysen' via nimble-users <nimble...@googlegroups.com> wrote:

Thanks Perry! I'm developing a simpler version of HMM with continuous measurements (which is not offered in nimbleEcology package I believe), but aiming at a more complicated model in the future, so your mentioning about  nimArray  is helping a lot. 

I was able to solve the problem by defining  probObs  as a vector (instead of a matrix, for now), the updated code is attached below. After fixing this, probObs can be defined deterministically as a normal density without warning.

However, I'm having a new issue emerged with the error message below,
[Note] Infinite values were detected in model variable: logProb_y.

While I'm figuring out if it arises from the forward algorithm (in nimbleFunction dmyHMM), which I highly suspect, or prior specification, any advise or help is greatly appreciate!

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
dmyHMM <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), # observations
                 probInit = double(1), # initial state probabilities
                 mu = double(1), # emission means
                 sigma = double(1), # emission standard deviations
                 probTrans = double(2), # transition probabilities
                 T_len = double(0, default = 0), # length of observation
                 log = integer(0, default = 0)
  ){
    ## at time point 1

    probObs <- numeric(2)

    # log forward probability
    alpha <- numeric(2)
    # accumulator
    alpha_out <- numeric(2)
   
    for (state in 1:2){
      probObs[state] <- dnorm(x[1], mean = mu[state], sd = sigma[state])
      alpha[state] <- log(probInit[state]) + log(probObs[state])
    }
    ## at time points 2:T
    for (time in 2:T_len) {
      for(state_in in 1:2){ # current state
        # emission density for observation at current time point
        probObs[state_in] <- dnorm(x[time], mean = mu[state_in], sd = sigma[state_in])
       
        for(state_out in 1:2){ # previous state
          alpha_out[state_out] <- alpha[state_out] + log(probTrans[state_out, state_in]) + log(probObs[state_in])
        }
        alpha[state_in] <- log(sum(exp(alpha_out[1:2])))
      }
    }
    logL <- log(sum(exp(alpha[1:2])))
    returnType(double(0))
    if (log) return(logL)
    return(exp(logL))
  }
)

On Tuesday, July 18, 2023 at 12:18:22 PM UTC-5 Perry de Valpine wrote:
Dear Jaysen,

Apologies that your message slipped by for a while with no attention. We try to keep up but sometimes we fall behind.  Thanks for posting the question.
Inside a nimbleFunction, you can create a new multivariate object with syntax similar to R. You can do
probObs <- nimArray(dim = c(3, 3, len)) # or you can use "array" and it will be converted to "nimArray"
Information on this and related features is in section 11.2 of the User Manual (r-nimble.org)

Also, there are versions of HMMs implemented in the nimbleEcology package, with a vignette that goes over how to use them. You might need something more specific, but I just wanted to point it out.

It looks like you are populating only diagonal elements of probObs[1:3, 1:3, time] for each time, so you could perhaps just create a vector and use component-wise multiplication instead of matrix multiplication (or perhaps you are building up to more complicated cases where you need the full matrix).

HTH.

Perry

Hi all,

Attached is a piece of code for a 2-state homogeneous Hidden Markov Model with Gaussian emission density. Basically, the observation y_t given hidden state s_t=i follows a Gaussian distribution with mean mu_i and standard deviation sigma_i, and the states have a transition probability matrix of gamma. 

However, an error was raised in the forward probability function, i.e., dmyHMM, with the message:
Error in probObs[state, state, time] <- (1/sqrt(2 * pi * (sigma[state])^2)) * : object 'probObs' not found

The probObs is meant to be defined as a matrix, with normal distribution densities on diagonals. Given the error message, I'm lost on where to define the probObs object. The attached code was one option that I tried, another try was to include probObs in the nimbleModel of homo.hmm, and treat it as a parameter in dmyHMM, but it also failed with a similar error message. 

Any suggestions, comments or questions are welcomed, thanks much in advance!

  run = function(x = double(1), # observations
                 probInit = double(1), # initial state probabilities
                 mu = double(1), # emission means
                 sigma = double(1), # emission standard deviations
                 probTrans = double(2), # transition probabilities
                 len = double(0, default = 0), # length of observation
                 log = integer(0, default = 0)
  ){
    for (time in 1:len) {
      # no deterministic assignment is allowed, but why?
      for (state in 1:3){
        #probObs[state, state, time] <- dnorm(x[time], mean = mu[state], sd = sigma[state])
        probObs[state, state, time] <- (1/sqrt(2*pi*(sigma[state])^2))*exp(-(x[time]-mu[state])^2/(2*sigma[state]^2))
      }
    }
   
    # forward probabilities
    ## at time point 1
    alpha <- probInit[1:3] %*% probObs[1:3, 1:3, 1]
    ## at time points 2:T
    for (time in 2:len) {
      # matrix multiplication:
      # forward at t = forward at t-1 %*% transition probabilities %*% emission probabilities
      alpha[1:3] <- (alpha[1:3] %*% probTrans[1:3,1:3]) %*% probObs[1:3, 1:3, time]
    }
    logL <- log(sum(alpha[1:3]))
    returnType(double(0))
    if (log) return(logL)
    return(exp(logL))
  }
)

  run = function(n = double(), # observations

    y <- s

      s[t] <- rcat(n = 1, prob = probTrans[s[t-1],1:2])
